title: Algorithmic bias in lending - the consumer protection angle
p1:
A computer can approve or reject your loan in seconds. But what happens when the system learns the wrong lessons?

Many people assume algorithms are always neutral because they rely on data, not human opinions.
p2:
The surprising truth: algorithms can repeat and even amplify existing unfair patterns. If past lending data reflects unequal access to credit, an AI system may unknowingly use those patterns when making future decisions.

The problem is not that machines are biased by nature. It is that they learn from the information they receive.
p3:
Consumer protection comes into play when people are denied fair opportunities without knowing why. Lenders using automated systems need transparency, regular testing, and safeguards to ensure decisions are accurate and fair.

A faster loan decision should not mean a less accountable one. Consumers deserve to know that technology is helping them, not silently creating new barriers.
conclusion: Should consumers have the right to know when an AI system influences a lending decision against them?
